purpose: Explain how internet subcultures, attention economies, archives, media, politics, classifiers, law enforcement, infrastructure and money can interact over time without presuming one hidden organization.
epistemic_firewall: Shared users, memes, donors, targets or audiences do not prove common command.
A platform is not identical to every community hosted on it.
A classification by SPLC, ADL, government, media or a forum is an attributed classification event, not an intrinsic property.
An indictment is an allegation, not a conviction.
A death associated in reporting with harassment is not automatically an adjudicated causal finding.
Farmer, Dog, Mud Dweller, Archon, Farm, Sektur, Swamp and Moloch are project analytical/mythic terms unless narrower factual conduct is separately established.
Terms such as trafficker, groomer, abuser or criminal require evidence for the specific conduct and are never generic synonyms for exploitation.

tim_thesis.summary: The project treats culture as a reproduction system. Platforms create places; repeated attention creates roles; archives create memory; money/status can reward repetition; media translates events into stories; politics and institutions can adopt or react to those stories; residue can then become input for the next cycle.
tim_thesis.chain: platform/seed -> encounter -> subculture -> role/status -> archive -> attention -> money/status -> media translation -> political/institutional translation -> consequence -> memory -> recurrence OR repair
tim_thesis.farm: Farm is the attention-production process: classify -> observe -> capture -> interpret -> archive -> redistribute -> renew observation.
tim_thesis.sektur: Sektur is social territory: recurring people, rivals, audiences, creators, lore, archives and roles. Historical Da Sektur remains a specific livestream-drama milieu before the project generalizes the term.
tim_thesis.swamp: Swamp is the wider environment: platforms, media, markets, politics, law, watchdogs, infrastructure and unresolved incentives. It is not a secret organization.
tim_thesis.mud: Mud is durable residue: old allegations, clips, labels, sanctions, legal records, reputational stories and archived conflict. Mud can preserve evidence or preserve distortion.

why_target_ecologies_persist.summary: Persistence usually needs reproduction, not a central mastermind.

mechanisms.mechanism: Different participants perform tiny tasks—watching, clipping, searching, posting, archiving, commenting, translating, identifying, moderating—so no single person bears the cost of maintaining the whole narrative.
Persistent threads, wikis, mirrors, screenshots and search indexes lower the cost of restarting attention years later.

Research on 231 Kiwi Farms threads found network users added narrative elements in at least 80% of threads; narrative continuation can keep targeted harassment alive, and removal requests can become new narrative material.
Insider knowledge, speed, access, technical skill, successful provocation, discovery and memorable jokes can become prestige within a scene even without direct payment.
Reaction itself can be the yield. A new post, response, appearance, court filing or attempted correction creates another observable event.

At larger layers attention can be monetized through ads, subscriptions, passes, donations, memberships, sponsorships, merchandise or political fundraising. Not every participant is paid, but the surrounding system can still assign economic value to attention.
Targets become commentators; commentators become targets; detractors become creators; archives become news sources. This prevents the ecology from depending on one stable center.
When a provider, host, CDN or platform acts, communities may migrate to new infrastructure. Cloudflare's 2022 Kiwi Farms block explicitly noted the site might move to other providers and return.

Cruel, obsessive or invasive conduct is not automatically one legally actionable offense. Federal cyberstalking law requires specified intent plus a course of conduct causing fear of serious injury or substantial emotional distress; other claims depend on threats, privacy, defamation, copyright, state law and jurisdiction.

U.S. law has generally provided online services significant protection from liability for third-party content under Section 230, while preserving liability for their own content/conduct and other exceptions. This can separate responsibility for user behavior from responsibility of the infrastructure.

A harmful dynamic can be publicly visible yet difficult to stop because evidence, jurisdiction, legal elements, platform rules, infrastructure ownership and institutional authority are distributed across different actors.

why_target_ecologies_persist.chris_chan_case_note: The Chris Chan/CWCki lineage is useful precisely because it demonstrates temporal persistence: documentation that begins around one highly visible person can become wiki memory, forum culture, a reusable target template and then a broader multi-target ecology. The project should describe documented actions and source provenance rather than treating every observer as one coordinated stalker.

platform_genealogy.current_observable: 4chan sells a Pass for $30/year or $60/3 years; the site's FAQ describes CDN/colocated infrastructure and large traffic.
Reddit reported $2.203B revenue for 2025, including $2.1B advertising revenue, with 121.4M daily active uniques in Q4.

platform_genealogy.harm_context: In 2019 attackers used 8chan to distribute/link manifestos around Christchurch, Poway and El Paso. Record this as platform use/distribution, not monocausal explanation.

platform_genealogy.genealogy: CWCki/CWCki Forums focused on Chris Chan before the forum broadened and became Kiwi Farms.
platform_genealogy.persistence_signal: A 2024 research study of 231 threads found sustained collaborative narrative escalation; an Open Measures summary reports more than 25% of targeted threads received replies for longer than 12 months.
platform_genealogy.infrastructure_event: Cloudflare blocked Kiwi Farms in September 2022 after saying threats had escalated to an immediate threat to human life; it also said the site could move providers and return.
platform_genealogy.harm_boundary: Major reporting has associated at least three suicides with people targeted by the community; preserve person-by-person causal status rather than turning that into a rhetorical body count.

flow_questions: Who receives money because attention persists?
Which nonprofits raise donations around threat/classification narratives?
Which political committees raise/spend around cultural conflict?
Which costs are unpaid volunteer labor rather than budgeted activity?

layers.meaning: original post, stream, filing, speech, video, dataset
thread/wiki/archive converts event into persistent searchable memory
streamers, internet bloodsports, commentary and satire convert events into performance and audience
professional reporting selects, verifies, contextualizes and republishes
SPLC, ADL and similar organizations turn observations into reports, categories, maps and public claims
campaigns, movements, officials and advocates turn cultural frames into mobilization, fundraising, policy or law
police, FBI, courts and regulators enter only under their own authority and evidentiary/legal standards

media_translation.fake_media_rule: Store 'fake media' as an attributed accusation about a specific report or claim. Record the disputed proposition, source chain, correction and evidence; never encode an outlet as intrinsically fake.

classifier_and_state_interfaces.method: SPLC says it uses publications, citizen reports, law enforcement, field sources, web postings and news reports; its hate-group category does not require criminal conduct.

classifier_and_state_interfaces.current_2026_case: DOJ indicted SPLC in April 2026 and later added charges/defendant in August over alleged concealed use of donated funds and fictitious accounts connected to paid informants. DOJ says these are allegations; SPLC pleaded not guilty and argued political retaliation.

classifier_and_state_interfaces.method: ADL says its Center on Extremism uses open-source intelligence and compiles incident/symbol datasets including the H.E.A.T. Map from news, government documents, victim reports, extremist sources and its own investigations.

accountability_gap.question: Why can something look obviously abusive to ordinary readers yet persist in public?
answer_parts: Moral wrong, platform-rule violation, tort, crime and human-rights concern are not identical legal categories.
A years-long pattern can consist of thousands of individually small acts spread across people and jurisdictions.
The archive preserves material even after original actors leave.
Intermediaries may have legal protection for third-party speech while still having their own moderation rules.
Law enforcement needs statutory elements and evidence, not merely public ugliness.
Infrastructure providers can intervene faster than courts, but deplatforming may cause migration rather than disappearance.
Targets may face a paradox: responding, correcting or requesting removal can create new attention.

darvo.definition: Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender.
darvo.project_use: Use as a testable response-pattern hypothesis when a challenged actor denies conduct, attacks the accuser and recasts themselves as the harmed party.
darvo.boundary: A denial is not automatically DARVO and DARVO language is not proof the underlying allegation is true.

case_protocol: Origin — when, by whom and for what initial purpose did the scene/platform begin?
Affordance — what behavior does the technology make cheap or rewarding?
Role — who watches, archives, reacts, moderates, classifies, funds, reports or becomes targeted?
Money — what revenue, donations, subscriptions, salaries, political spending or infrastructure payments are actually documented?
Memory — which archives let old material reactivate?
Escalation — what new event or narrative element renews attention?
Media — who transforms raw events into entertainment, journalism, advocacy or political framing?
Institution — which classifier, employer, platform, host, police agency, FBI office, court or regulator enters?
Legal status — allegation, platform rule, civil claim, charge, conviction, official finding or unresolved?
Harm — what happened to the person, and what causal level is actually supported?
Repair — what correction, exit, de-escalation, record repair or incentive change reduced recurrence?
